claims.head: The Red Wings like DeBrincat’s line against Wennberg’s
claims.call: The Red Wings’ L2 (DeBrincat, Finnie and Brandsegg-Nygård) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sharks’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Red Wings keep sending DeBrincat’s line (DeBrincat, Finnie and Brandsegg-Nygård) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Todd McLellan keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Sharks’ second line is Toffoli, Wennberg and Marchment.

claims.gist: At home, Todd McLellan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Sharks’ second line.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 46%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 5 of their last 7 games, including the last one. Keegan Kolesar takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Axel Sandin-Pellikka is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Johansson and Chiarot.

DET.head: The Red Wings have a lot going for them
DET.body: Detroit has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Sharks can make it interesting if they get good looks.
